model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 35% to 65%, with major gridlines every 5 percentage points. The “Base” method (black solid line with circle markers) starts at ~38% ACC at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to ~44% at 10⁴. The “FT” method (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins at ~40% and rises to ~48%. The “IKE” method (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~43% and reaches ~49.5%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~44% and climbs to ~56.5%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~44% and increases to ~55%. The “ROME” method (green line with square markers) begins at ~51% and steadily rises to ~66.5% at 10⁴, consistently outperforming all other methods across the entire range.
